properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent and nothing is settled.

HIS IDEA, in his words: "there are 2 sets of linked projects. 1) dynograph-foundation : reflow2 : flo2 and 2) dynograph-foundation : storyflow. the key (but obvious) is that dynograph-foundation is used in both. probably need to do a git pull on both dev_storyflow and storyflow repos on this machine, but all repos/reflow2 projects are on this machine. this would really stress linking multiple projects. also as we discuss making changes to dynograph-foundation, we can't make these in isolation to storyflow."

⭐ IDEA A — THE FOUR-CORNER RUN ITSELF. `dec:linked-repos-poc` composed THREE designs on 2026-08-06 (reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation) and it worked: zero skipped edges, ids namespaced, one true positive. What has never run is BOTH ARMS AT ONCE with the shared upstream in the middle. That is a different test, not a bigger one: three designs in a line exercise linking; two chains meeting at a shared node exercise whether the tooling can see a diamond at all.

🛑 IDEA B — MEASURED TODAY, IT WOULD HIT TWO KNOWN BLOCKERS, AND BOTH WERE PREDICTED. State of the four corners, read 2026-08-21:

  reflow2               2868 nodes   graph_id `reflow2`                published 3 / required 9 / internal 6
  dynograph-foundation   179 nodes   graph_id `dynograph-foundation`   published 15 / required 0
  flo2                   109 nodes   graph_id `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`       published 5 / required 1 / internal 1
  dev_storyflow         1373 nodes   graph_id `reflow2`  🔴            published 0 / required 0 (44 internal, 9 unset)

  (1) THE graph_id COLLISION IS REAL AND STILL THERE. dev_storyflow's export and its `.reflow2/graph.id.json` both carry graph_id `reflow2`; only `label` says `dev_storyflow`. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` called this out on 2026-08-09 as "a collision waiting to happen", and nothing has changed. `compose_and_analyse` takes an explicit namespace so a run can be forced through, but anything keying on graph_id sees two designs claiming to be reflow2.
  (2) STORYFLOW'S ARM IS UNLABELLED. 53 interfaces, none `required`, none `published` — the exact state reflow2 was in before PR #130. Pairing matches complements, so storyflow's arm of the diamond CANNOT pair with anything today. A four-corner run would produce a real seam on one arm and an honest zero on the other, and the zero would need reading correctly.

⭐ IDEA C — HIS SECOND SENTENCE IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE, AND IT IS ALREADY AN OPEN QUESTION. "We can't make these in isolation to storyflow" is `dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked` — B and D both depend on A, and A's blast radius stops at its own graph. Stated as a working constraint rather than a question, which is new: he is describing how he intends to work, not asking whether it is a problem.

⭐ IDEA D — AND THE PRIOR RECORD SAYS A NAIVE DIAMOND CHECK WOULD REPORT ALL-CLEAR. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` measured it: reflow2 consumes dynograph as a RUST LIBRARY API (5 required interfaces), storyflow consumes it as a REST API (6 interfaces). DISJOINT SURFACES over one shared implementation. So "do B and D require the same interface?" answers NO and means nothing. The question that would have caught the real incident is "did the change reach BELOW both published surfaces into shared implementation" — which is about dynograph's OWN internals and is answerable only inside dynograph's graph.

⭐ IDEA E — AND TODAY'S FINDING IS EXACTLY THAT LAYER. `fact:the-storage-seam-is-published-in-design-and-private-in-code`: `ifc:kv-backend` is the ONE node in any of these four designs that names the shared substrate beneath both consumers' surfaces, and its design says `published` while its code says `pub(crate)`. If a four-corner run is meant to find the diamond's real risk, that node is where the risk lives — not at the paired interfaces, which are exactly the places a change CANNOT reach both consumers.

📋 IDEA F — CHEAP PREREQUISITES, offered as observations rather than a plan. A `git pull` on both storyflow repos, as he suggests. dev_storyflow's export lives at `.reflow2/design.export.json` rather than under `docs/design/`, so it is not a committed record the way the other three are, and it was written by reflow2 0.26.1 while dynograph-foundation's was written by 0.16.0 — a four-way compose would span three writer versions. `dec:linked-repos-poc` already showed cross-version composition surviving eight minor versions with nothing dropped, which is evidence and not proof.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT PROPOSED HERE: changing anything in storyflow or dev_storyflow. AGENTS.md rule 6 forbids landing work there without Anthony's word, and declaring storyflow's `required` interfaces — the step that would make its arm pair — is design about a project this session has not been asked to touch.

DISTINCT FROM the three nodes the guard surfaced. `dec:linked-repos-poc` RAN a three-design composition and is about whether the mechanism works; this asks whether both arms together are a different test. The diamond FACT measured the shape of the two consumers' surfaces on one dated occasion; this proposes an action and records what it would hit today. `dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked` asks how notification should work; this asks whether composing everything at once is how you would find out you needed it.
properties.name: OPEN — should BOTH dependency chains be composed at once as a four-corner stress test, and is the shared upstream changeable without storyflow in the room?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as ideas so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed as intent.

Searched the graph BEFORE writing, which is the lesson from earlier this session — `fact:the-seam-report-half-of-the-poc-finally-ran` records re-deriving an analysis the design already held. That search is why ideas C, D and E point at existing nodes rather than restating them.

The state table in idea B was read today rather than recalled, because the last two times this was reasoned about from memory the numbers had moved.
